title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
dek: A successful launch begins a chain of deployments, calibrations, public data releases, and scientific tests that can be observed rather than merely anticipated.
trackingTerms: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope status
whyTracked: Roman has a precise technical baseline, near-term engineering gates, measurable scientific performance, and an unusually strong open-data promise.

current.assessment: Roman has completed its first mid-course correction, deployed its high-gain antenna and aperture cover, and powered on the Coronagraph Instrument. Early commissioning is proceeding through documented milestones, while Wide Field Instrument activation, full calibration, L2 insertion, and first public observations remain unresolved.
current.nextReviewTrigger: Review immediately for Wide Field Instrument activation, a commissioning anomaly, L2 insertion, completed commissioning, or first public observations.

openQuestions: Will the remaining commissioning milestones, including Wide Field Instrument activation and calibration, succeed?
When will first science images and survey data be released?
Will immediate public access produce substantial research beyond the mission’s planned programs?

watchFor.description: Wide Field Instrument activation and commissioning tests
watchFor.trigger: NASA reports instrument power-on, checkout results, calibration progress, or an anomaly.
NASA reports orbital insertion or completion of the commissioning campaign.

watchFor.description: First science images and initial data release
watchFor.trigger: NASA releases the first processed observations.

observations.headline: Point-zero observation
observations.summary: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on August 30, 2026, beginning a roughly three-month deployment, calibration, and commissioning period before planned first science images in early 2027.

observations.headline: Admitted to The Wake pilot
observations.summary: Admitted because a single launch opens into a long sequence of observable engineering, scientific, and institutional outcomes.

observations.headline: Early commissioning milestones succeed
observations.summary: NASA reported that Roman completed its first mid-course correction, deployed the high-gain antenna and aperture cover, and powered on the Coronagraph Instrument. These are successful early commissioning milestones; instrument calibration, Wide Field Instrument activation, L2 insertion, and full commissioning remain ahead.
